messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-10T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the items we said we'd follow up on: 

1) PII & data classification
- You confirmed that PHI and user-identifiable PII (name, email, MRN) will be sent to inference only when explicitly required by the application.
- Primary ask: confirm whether any unmasked PHI may be sent to the model for enrichment or transformation workflows.

2) Data retention & logging
- You want logs (request/response metadata) retained for 7 years for audit purposes; raw request contents that contain PHI should not be stored beyond processing unless explicitly opted-in.
- Clarify retention windows and whether logs must be stored inside customer-managed storage.

3) Data residency & network boundaries
- Preference for Private (VPC) deployment in our US region with no public internet egress.
- On-prem / air-gapped option was discussed as a possible need for subset of workloads.

4) Controls & evidence
- You'll need SOC 2 snapshot, network diagram showing peering and egress controls, and our security questionnaire responses.

Next steps (what I can deliver):
- Attached: network-diagram.pdf (high-level VPC peering options) and acme_qs_answers.xlsx (answers to the security questions we discussed).
- I will also attach a current redwood SOC 2 snapshot by EOD tomorrow.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute technical deep-dive with our infra/security lead (Laura) to confirm egress allowlist and retention implementation.

Can you confirm the "no internet egress" requirement applies to ALL inference nodes (including health-checks/metrics) and whether you anticipate any outbound integrations (S3, object storage) that need explicit allowlisting?

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf, acme_qs_answers.xlsx

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Bob Lee <bob.lee@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-05-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth — Private VPC data flow & privacy follow-up

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. A few clarifications from the security team: 

- "No internet egress" must apply to inference workloads that process PHI. We can allow monitoring/metrics telemetry to egress to our internal monitoring endpoints only; anything that goes to a public SaaS endpoint needs to be blocked or routed through our proxy.
- We need the network diagram to show NAT/eBPF behavior for health checks and to confirm that metadata logging (request IDs, timestamps) can be exported to our existing SIEM inside the VPC.
- Retention: 7 years for audit logs is required, but raw request payloads containing PHI must either be retained in customer-managed encrypted storage or not stored at all.
- On-prem requirement: we are evaluating two workloads — one can be in a customer VPC with strict egress allowlist, the other may need to be on-prem/air-gapped behind our firewall. Please confirm whether Redwood Private supports a fully air-gapped install (no outbound license checks) and what the operational patching cadence would look like for that deployment model.

Also can you provide a current SOC 2 report or a snapshot that we can share with our procurement team? Finally, please send IP ranges and any outbound ports your service needs so our network team can prepare allowlists.

Appreciate it —

Regards,
Alice Johnson
Director, Security Engineering
Acme Health

Hi Alice —

Attached are the artifacts you requested: network-diagram.pdf (detailed VPC peering + optional on-prem network flow), acme_qs_answers.xlsx (security questionnaire answers), and redwood_SOC2_snapshot.pdf (current SOC 2 summary).

Short answers inline to your bullets above:
- No internet egress: Supported. Our Private deployment can be configured with no public egress; outbound traffic can be restricted to customer-managed endpoints only. Health checks/metrics can be routed to your internal endpoints via VPC peering.
- Logging/retention: We support exporting logs to customer-managed encrypted S3/GCS or to your SIEM over private connectivity. By default Redwood does not persist raw request payloads containing PHI unless the customer enables storage for specific workflows.
- Air-gapped/on-prem: We support an on-prem package for regulated workloads. Air-gapped: yes, however it requires an initial secure bundle for installation and a controlled release process for patches (we publish security patches quarterly by default; emergency patches are available under an enterprise support SLA).

IP ranges and minimal outbound ports are included on page 3 of the attached network-diagram.pdf. If the network team prefers, I can create a shrink-wrapped list of CIDRs and ports for your firewall team.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical deep-dive with Laura (our infra/security lead) and your network lead to confirm the allowlist and retention model. Are you available Tue 2026-05-19 at 10:00 AM PT?

Thanks —

Marissa

Attachments: network-diagram.pdf, acme_qs_answers.xlsx, redwood_SOC2_snapshot.pdf
